about:
Smith operates as an independent electronic-component distributor headquartered in Houston, Texas, with additional global hubs in Amsterdam and Hong Kong. The company was founded in 1984 and has accumulated more than four decades of experience navigating the semiconductor supply chain. No specific founder names or ownership designations such as family- or veteran-owned are disclosed in public materials.

The firm provides procurement, supply-chain management, and quality-testing services for electronic components and peripherals. Its service portfolio includes vendor-managed inventory, obsolescence management, excess-inventory recovery, custom supply-chain programs, and a proprietary trading platform called SmithTrade™. Smith reports shipping approximately 6.5 million parts daily, capturing 15 million high-resolution component images via its Argus™ visual-inspection AI since 2025, and operating five global operational facilities with in-house testing laboratories on three continents. Revenue for the first half of 2026 exceeded $6 billion.

Smith serves customers across aerospace and defense, automation, automotive, computing, consumer electronics, data center, e-commerce, education, gaming, IoT, medical, mobile, and oil and gas sectors. Its aerospace and defense work is supported by ISO/IEC 17025 AS6171 accreditation for authenticity testing.

The company differentiates itself through its 'Intelligent Distribution' model and a quality framework built on four pillars—Comprehensive, Consistent, Continuous, and Certified—supplemented by proprietary software, global logistics hubs, and a team of developers that customize IT integrations for each program.
